full_judgment: 4. The defendant-opposite party No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations in the plaint contending, inter alias that the entire land in the suit plot measuring 1080 ajutangsha was the khas land of the government. Accordingly, the government settled the same with different persons from time to time and one Nanda Kishore Shah being one of the settlement holders sold his share in the land in the suit plot to one Fazle Rashid by a registered deed No. 7604 dated 16-12-52 and subsequently, the father of the said defendant-opposite party No.1 purchased the same from Fazle Rashid by a registered sale deed No. 5334 dated 14-9-53 and got the same duly recorded in his name and paid rents. The defendant opposite party No.1 inherited the said land after the death of his father and had his name recorded in SA Khatian in respect of the said land and since then he has been owning and possessing specifically one third share of the land in the suit plot. The defendant-opposite party No.1 having subsequently learnt that the suit plot was government khas land prayed for regular settlement of the same and defendant Nos. 2-4 accordingly, settled one third share of the land of the suit plot with the defendant opposite party No.1 on 2-12-81 and since then he has been owning and possessing the same.
